name: Wi-Fi signal strength and link speed
plain: Android reads signal and link speed with no prompt; iOS gives signal strength only with the Wi-Fi entitlement.
meaning: Gives a rough distance from the router and speed tier. Can be used with BSSID to locate the person inside a home.

android.note: RSSI -100 to -30 dBm; link speed up to 2400 Mbps and beyond

limits.headline: Can see Wi-Fi signal strength and speed on Android; iPhone needs special approval
limits.user_action: Nothing on Android. On iPhone only approved apps can do it
can: Get signal strength in dBm on Android
See link speed up to 2400 Mbps and more, the frequency and Wi-Fi generation
Get a normalized signal value on iPhone with the Wi-Fi entitlement
cannot: See signal strength on iPhone without the special Apple entitlement
See other people's networks or passwords
limits.reach_label: Signal and speed of your Wi-Fi
limits.differs: Android shows dBm and speed with a normal permission. iPhone needs a special Apple entitlement and gives a normalized value.

story.what_it_is: An app can read your Wi-Fi signal strength and speed.
story.for_you: You do not see it. A video call app may warn you that your signal is weak. It also tells the app about how far you are from the router.
story.for_makers: Makers use signal strength to adjust quality and to warn users. It can help guess where you are in a home, especially together with the network ID. It is more open on Android than on iPhone.

use_cases.example: A video call app drops to audio only when Wi-Fi gets weak.
A cloud gaming app shows a signal meter and warns you about lag.
A router app shows which rooms have weak Wi-Fi and suggests a better spot for the router.
A speed test app shows link speed and signal in dBm.
A tracker combines signal strength with the router ID to guess where you stand in a home.
A security app notes a sudden drop in signal as a clue of a fake hotspot nearby.

story.android_note: Android apps read signal and link speed with no prompt on current versions.
story.ios_note: iPhone gives signal strength only to apps with the Wi-Fi information entitlement.
